text: Each member also holds a signed mandate for their own agent: a charge limit, an expiry, and rules. It's our own AP2-style mandate, with a server-attested signature.
Round three runs on its own. Five charges complete, each confirmed through the PayPal Agent Toolkit. Ravi's charge is declined, and it's labelled sandbox-injected.
Now the members' agents answer, each inside its mandate. Tomas's accepts an earlier turn. Ravi's asks him first. Four of six vote yes, and Priya taps once.
The ledger checks out, and PayPal Payouts sends Dev the pot, net of fees. Those are PayPal's own IDs on the receipt.
A two hundred thirty dollar charge, over the two hundred dollar mandate, is refused before PayPal is called.
Round four is clean: six charges, one payout, and Priya typed nothing.
Under the hood, the model proposes, a policy engine decides, and humans and member agents act inside signed mandates.
On PayPal: Vault, Orders, Payouts, Invoicing through the Agent Toolkit, Webhooks and Balances. The tools sit behind an MCP server. A free model can drive it; this take used rules mode.
In a hundred rules-mode runs, ninety-five percent of proposals were charter-legal, and zero illegal actions executed.
It's sandbox only, the buffer is optional, we make no credit claims, and our mandates are AP2-style, not AP2 support.
